summary: Magic Maze is a real-time cooperative puzzle where each player controls a limited action (move north, move south, escalator, search) across all four heroes, and the core twist is that verbal communication is banned once the sand timer starts, forcing players to grab each other's pawns and point frantically instead. It plays fast and chaotic, with tension coming from the ban on talking rather than from the maze-building itself.
praised: Unique communication-limit gimmick that creates genuinely funny, tense moments
Fast setup and short playtime, good as a filler or icebreaker
Scales unusually well, including a solo mode controlling multiple heroes
Modular board and expansions add variety
criticised: Can create real frustration or friction for players who dislike being unable to speak
One dominant/fast player can effectively solve it for the group, reducing others to spectators
Puzzle logic is fairly light and repetitive across plays
Not very forgiving for very young or new-to-boardgames players despite low weight

interaction.kind: silent cooperative coordination, non-verbal signaling and pawn-grabbing

scoring.why: the group either gets all heroes to the exit before the timer/pyramid runs out or loses together, with no individual scoring

similar: Escape: The Curse of the Temple
